n: Construction of the temple begins in Solomon’s fourth year, about 480 years after the Exodus. The date links the temple to Israel’s deliverance from Egypt: freedom led to a house where God could dwell among His people.

f.w: the four hundred and eightieth year
f.g: Possibly a symbolic number (12 generations of 40 years) or an exact count; scholars differ on dating the Exodus.
Ziv, the second month of the year, in April–May — “the month of brightness” or flowers.

n: The main building is about 90 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 45 feet high — not huge by modern standards, but magnificent in materials and meaning. It doubles the tabernacle’s dimensions.

f.g: A cubit was about 18 inches (45 cm), the length from elbow to fingertip.
60 cubits.

n: A porch, or entrance hall, extends across the front of the building.

f.g: Hebrew ’ulam — a vestibule at the temple’s entrance, facing east.

n: High, narrow windows let in light — probably latticed openings near the top of the walls.

f.g: Possibly windows with recessed frames, or latticed openings.

n: Rooms are built in stories along the outside walls of the main hall and the inner sanctuary — likely storerooms for temple supplies and treasures.

f.g: Hebrew devir — the innermost room, the Holy of Holies, where God “spoke.”
Side rooms, arranged in three stories.

n: Each story of side rooms is a bit wider than the one below, because the temple wall steps inward as it rises, providing ledges for the beams so they don’t have to be inserted into the sacred walls.

f.g: Lowest.
Ledges or offsets in the wall.

n: The stones were cut and finished at the quarry, so no hammer, axe, or iron tool was heard at the temple site. The house of God rose in reverent quiet. Many see a lesson here: God shapes His people in the world so they can fit peacefully into His holy house.

f.w: neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron

n: The entrance to the side rooms is on the south side, with a winding staircase or ladder leading to the upper floors.

f.g: The south side, if facing east toward the entrance.
Possibly a spiral staircase, or trapdoors and ladders.

n: Solomon completes the structure and roofs it with cedar beams and planks.

f.g: Roofed.

n: The side rooms, each story about 7.5 feet high, are attached to the temple with cedar beams.
In the midst of the construction, the word of the Lord comes to Solomon.

f.w: the word of the LORD came to Solomon
f.g: Perhaps through a prophet, or by direct revelation.

n: God reminds him that the building alone is not enough. If Solomon keeps His commandments, God will fulfill His promises to David. The temple’s value depends on the faithfulness of the people.

f.w: if thou wilt walk in my statutes

n: Then God will dwell among Israel and never forsake His people — the true purpose of any temple.

f.w: I will dwell among the children of Israel

n: Solomon finishes building the house — the narrator repeats it for emphasis.
Inside, the stone walls are paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling, and the floor is laid with cypress planks.

f.g: Cypress or juniper boards.

n: At the back, a cedar partition walls off a 30-foot section to form the inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

f.g: The Holy of Holies, where the ark was kept and God’s presence dwelt.

n: The main hall in front of it, the Holy Place, is about 60 feet long.

f.g: Hebrew hekal — the main hall or Holy Place, in front of the inner sanctuary.

n: The cedar paneling is carved with gourds and open flowers; no stone is visible inside. The garden imagery may recall Eden, the first place where God walked with humankind.

f.g: Knobs — probably gourd-shaped ornaments.

n: The inner sanctuary is prepared to hold the ark of the covenant.

f.w: the ark of the covenant of the LORD

n: The Most Holy Place is a perfect cube, 30 feet in each direction, overlaid with pure gold. The altar of incense is also covered in gold. In Revelation, the holy city is likewise a cube.

f.w: twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in the height
the altar which was of cedar
f.g: The altar of incense, which stood before the inner sanctuary.

n: Solomon overlays the interior with gold and stretches gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary. A veil likely hung there too, separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy.
The entire interior and the incense altar are covered with gold. Gold, which does not tarnish, symbolized purity and the glory of God.

f.w: the whole house he overlaid with gold

n: Two huge cherubim, 15 feet tall and carved from olive wood, are made for the inner sanctuary.

f.g: Winged heavenly beings that guarded the way to God’s presence.
Olive wood, perhaps wild olive or oleaster.

n: Each cherub’s wingspan is 15 feet, with each wing measuring 7.5 feet.
The second cherub has the same size and shape as the first — perfect symmetry.
Both stand 15 feet tall.
The cherubim stand side by side; their outer wings touch the side walls and their inner wings meet in the middle. The ark would rest beneath their outstretched wings, as if under God’s throne.
The cherubim are overlaid with gold.
All the walls are carved with cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers — angels and garden imagery suggesting a return to the presence of God, as in Eden.
Even the floor of both rooms is overlaid with gold.

f.g: In the inner sanctuary and the outer room.

n: The entrance to the inner sanctuary has doors of olive wood with a five-sided doorframe.

f.w: a fifth part of the wall
f.g: The Hebrew may mean a five-sided or pentagonal frame.

n: The olive-wood doors are carved with cherubim, palms, and flowers, all overlaid with gold.
The main entrance has doorposts of olive wood with a four-sided frame.

f.w: a fourth part of the wall
f.g: Possibly a four-sided (rectangular) frame.

n: Its two doors are of cypress, each made of two folding panels.

f.g: Panels of a door.

n: They too are carved with cherubim, palms, and flowers and overlaid with fitted gold.
The inner courtyard wall is built with three layers of cut stone topped by one layer of cedar beams — a technique that may have helped buildings withstand earthquakes.

f.g: The priests’ court around the temple, where the altar of sacrifice stood.

n: The foundation was laid in Solomon’s fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
The temple is finished seven years later, in the month of Bul, in every detail. Seven years — the number of completeness — fits the building of God’s house.

f.g: The eighth month, October–November, the time of autumn rains.
About seven and a half years by exact count; seven also echoes the seven days of creation.
